data.proposal:
Hi everyone! I’ve dug into why the system couldn’t lock in flights for all six of you, and it comes down to two overlapping issues:

1. 4-hour arrival window:  
   • With people coming from Mumbai, Chicago, San Francisco, and New York, the cheapest same-day routings land anywhere from mid-morning on Sept 17 (Priya) to mid-afternoon (Yuki/Carlos). That’s an 8-10-hour spread—double the 4-hour limit—so the solver keeps rejecting otherwise workable itineraries.  

2. Two tight personal constraints that magnify the gap:  
   • Marcus can’t depart Chicago before 10:00 on Sept 16, which rules out the early trans-Atlantic flights that would help him arrive earlier.  
   • Aisha’s $350 cap from JFK is about $75–$100 below every flight that would sync with the rest of the group.

A concrete fix that WOULD let us book everyone:

A. Widen the “land-within” window from 4 hours to 8 hours (e.g., everyone on the ground in Barcelona between 08:00 and 16:00 on Sept 17).  
B. Marcus: allow an earlier departure—either late on Sept 15 (overnight) or anytime after 06:00 on Sept 16.  
C. Aisha: raise your flight budget from $350 to at least $450 (current matching fares are $420–$440).  

If we can agree to those three tweaks, the engine finds six itineraries that:

• Keep everyone on one travel day (departing Sept 15 evening or Sept 16).  
• Put all of you in Barcelona by midday/early afternoon on Sept 17 (window ≈ 6 hours).  
• Stay within everyone else’s stated budgets (Priya $600, Yuki $900, Carlos $500, Emma $600).  

Could we get a quick thumbs-up (or proposed adjustments) from:

• Marcus – OK to leave as early as 06:00 on Sept 16 or fly overnight on Sept 15?  
• Aisha – OK to lift your cap to $450?  
• Everyone – OK if we broaden the shared arrival window to 8 hours (roughly 08:00-16:00 on Sept 17)?

Let me know, and I can rerun the search immediately!
